# A test counts a looped `#id` read whole, as the interpreter counts the copies
# the loop rendered: `c.title.length()`, again after a write changes the list,
# one inner loop's `c.g.cell[1].length()`, and a sngl:seq sequence's. Every
# compiled target answers it with the loop's own count, read through the
# instance (answerTestCopyCount); before, it was `c.title undefined` on Go and
# `undefined.length` on html, where `c.title[1]` built.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import seq "sngl:seq"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component grid ui.node {
    var rows = [["a", "b"], ["c"]]
    var n = 4
    ui.vbox {
        for var row = rows {
            for var cell = row {
                ui.text #cell(value=cell)
            }
        }
        for var i = seq.step(n, 0, -2) {
            ui.text #down(value="{i}")
        }
    }
}

component card ui.node {
    var names = ["a", "b", "c"]
    ui.vbox {
        for var n = names {
            ui.text #title(value=n)
        }
        grid #g
    }
}

func testLoopedIDWhole(t test.Test, c card) {
    t.assert(c.title.length() == 3)
    t.assert(c.title[1].value == "b")
    c.names = ["x"]
    t.assert(c.title.length() == 1)
}

func testNestedAndCountedLoops(t test.Test, c card) {
    t.assert(c.g.cell.length() == 2)
    t.assert(c.g.cell[0].length() == 2)
    t.assert(c.g.cell[1].length() == 1)
    t.assert(c.g.down.length() == 2)
    c.g.n = 5
    t.assert(c.g.down.length() == 3)
}

ui.window {
    card
}
